title: GPTScan: Detecting Logic Vulnerabilities in Smart Contracts by Combining GPT with Program Analysis

key_numbers.metric: Static confirmation filters false-positive candidate functions

structure_gain: Static (dataflow) confirmation of GPT-recognized key variables/statements filters 65.84% of false-positive candidates on the same GPT-3.5-turbo pipeline (647->221 functions, Sec 5.3 Table 4) — a same-model component ablation isolating the symbolic stage, consistent with the corpus's RepoAudit-style neuro-symbolic isolation coding.
confound_note: RQ3 ablation holds model (GPT-3.5-turbo), prompts, and candidate set constant and varies only the presence of static confirmation — component-isolated; cross-dataset precision differences (90.91% vs 57.14%) reflect dataset difficulty, not the ablation.
threats_to_datum: Record restored after a screening-to-extraction handoff loss (screened include in decisions_chunk1 under its OpenAlex/DOI identity, which carried no arxiv_id; documented in decisions_adjudication.json D2). Author-extracted and author-verified directly against arxiv.org/html/2308.03314 (2026-08-30); not covered by the blind second coding (corpus coverage 67/68), disclosed in Appendix B.

title: SCALE: Constructing Structured Natural Language Comment Trees for Software Vulnerability Detection

key_numbers.value: 62.85% (SCALE) vs 56.04% best baseline (UniXcoder; CodeBERT 49.10% is the worst, not best, baseline)

key_numbers.metric: CodeBERT F1 gain from SCT-enhanced representation

structure_gain: SCALE (AST + LLM-generated comment tree) improves F1 by 1.17-13.47 points over best pre-trained/LLM baseline across three datasets (Table 3); RQ4 ablation shows removing SCT-Enhanced Representation module degrades performance.
confound_note: Main comparison (Table 3) varies both representation and underlying model architecture (SCALE-augmented UniXcoder vs. CodeBERT/CodeT5/ChatGPT baselines); RQ4 ablation (with/without SCTC, with/without SER) isolates representation components while holding the base encoder fixed.
threats_to_datum: Self-reported: limited to C/C++ (no Java/Python generalization claim), only 11 structured rules covering 4 statement categories, and evaluation restricted to models under 1B parameters (Section 6.2).

title: Code Vulnerability Repair with Large Language Model using Context-Aware Prompt Tuning
structure_gain: Repair success rises from 15% (no context) to 63% (full context-aware prompt combining CWE knowledge + structured code-context cues), a >4x improvement, same LLM (Copilot) throughout (Table I).
confound_note: Same LLM (GitHub Copilot) and same 156 snippets across all conditions; only prompt content varies in staged fashion (no context -> vulnerability disclosure -> CWE detail -> full structured context), isolating context amount as the manipulated variable.
threats_to_datum: No explicit threats-to-validity section; single commercial LLM (Copilot) tested, small custom dataset (156 snippets) with manual success labeling, and programming language not explicitly stated (examples appear C/C++).

title: RepoAudit: An Autonomous LLM-Agent for Repository-Level Code Auditing
datasets: custom benchmark of 15 real-world C/C++ projects
9 additional high-profile OSS projects (real-world validation set)
structure_gain: Ablations, same agent: no-abstraction precision 40.38% (21TP/31FP) and no-validator 51.28% (40TP/38FP) vs full RepoAudit 78.43% (Table 6).
confound_note: Table 6 ablations vary only one component at a time (program abstraction on/off; validator on/off) holding the LLM and benchmark fixed -- a clean representation/verification-only ablation.
threats_to_datum: Interprocedural analysis is explicitly bounded to a maximum calling-context depth of 4 functions and the authors state RepoAudit 'is not sound' for longer call chains; residual false positives/negatives from LLM hallucination persist despite the validator.

title: Identifying Helpful Context for LLM-based Vulnerability Repair: A Preliminary Study
venue: EASE 2025 (28th->29th International Conference on Evaluation and Assessment in Software Engineering, ACM proceedings, Istanbul)

key_numbers.metric: repair rate per run (Short+CVE+Manual vs GPT-4o baseline)
avg repair rate, CWE vs CVE context
Top-3 prompt ensemble, distinct vulns fixed
key_numbers.value: 26/42 (61.9%) vs original baseline 17/42 (40.4%) vs GPT-4o reproduction 19/42 (45.2%)

structure_gain: Combining a CVE-derived repair guideline with manually extracted repository context (Short+CVE Hints+Manual) achieves the best single-prompt result (18-14-17 across 3 runs) vs GPT-4o baseline (11-12-14), same GPT-4o-2024-08-06 model, temperature 0.01 throughout (Table 1).
confound_note: The central ablation (Table 1) holds the LLM (GPT-4o) and temperature fixed while varying only prompt context content (code visibility, docs, CWE, CVE, manual hints) -- a clean representation-only ablation; the separate GPT-4 vs GPT-4o comparison confounds model version with non-identical evaluation methodology (Sec 5).
threats_to_datum: Authors' own stated threats: Java-only generalizability, GPT-4o non-determinism even at temp 0.01, manual context extraction introduces subjectivity, and the GPT-4 vs GPT-4o comparison used non-identical evaluation methodology (Sec 5).

title: VerilogLAVD: LLM-Aided Rule Generation for Vulnerability Detection in Verilog
datasets: custom (77 Verilog designs, 12 CWE types, mutation-synthesized)

key_numbers.metric: Illegal rule-usage rate with validation FSM

structure_gain: VeriPG graph (AST + control/data dependency) plus LLM-generated traversal rules improves F1 over LLM+external-knowledge baseline by 0.32 (GPT-4o: 0.57 vs 0.25) and 0.16 (DeepSeek-V3: 0.50 vs 0.34), same backbone LLMs held fixed (Table 2).
confound_note: Same two backbone LLMs (GPT-4o, DeepSeek-V3) used across LLM-only, LLM+Knowledge, and VerilogLAVD arms; representation/context is the varied factor (raw code -> raw code+CWE text -> VeriPG graph+generated rules), though the full pipeline adds a rule-generation-and-traversal step beyond passive context.
threats_to_datum: No explicit threats-to-validity section; small dataset (77 designs, largely mutation-synthesized rather than real-world), single-module scope only, and no experimental comparison against traditional RTL security tools (e.g., Spyglass) due to unavailable code.

title: Multi-Agent Taint Specification Extraction for Vulnerability Detection
datasets: Known Vulnerability Dataset (172 total / 162 test, from Brito et al.)
OSS Dataset (102 npm packages from top 5,000 by SourceRank)
structure_gain: LLM-derived taint specs (sources/sinks + repaired call graph) raise recall from 0% (CodeQL baseline, ruleset R1) to 65.43% (106/162) on known vulnerabilities; ablation (RQ3/Table IV) shows 76.4% of catches needed only custom sources/sinks while 23.6% additionally needed call-graph repair.
confound_note: CodeQL analysis engine held constant across rulesets R1-R7; varied factor is which LLM-derived representation component (sources/sinks vs repaired call graph vs both) is supplied, reasonably isolating representation contribution, though LLM backbone differs slightly per agent role (GPT-4 vs GPT-4-mini).
threats_to_datum: Self-reported: callback-mediated taint propagation unmodeled, TICR can miss calls across intra-procedural gaps, JS/npm-only scope, 1M-token limit excludes 21 large packages, dataset from June 2021 may not generalize to current code, and OSS filtering biases toward packages with prior GHSA records.

title: Vulnerability Detection with Interprocedural Context in Multiple Languages: Assessing Effectiveness and Cost of Modern LLMs
structure_gain: Adding interprocedural context (callee/caller code) DEGRADED performance for most models -- e.g. GPT-4.1 Mini F1 dropped 0.8608 -> 0.6753 (Code-Only vs Code+Callees, C, same model/prompt/temperature=0); only Claude Haiku 4.5 was robust. Token usage nearly doubled (+102%) without proportional gains.
confound_note: Clean representation-only ablation: identical model, prompt template, temperature=0, and output length across conditions -- only the amount/type of interprocedural context varies (Code-Only vs +Callees vs +Callers).
threats_to_datum: Dataset has no negative (non-vulnerable) examples, so 'accuracy' is effectively recall; possible training-data contamination from public CVE reports; single-evaluator manual scoring of explanations (RQ4); C++ sample sizes as small as 5-18 excluded from statistical testing.

title: Representation Matters: An Empirical Study of Program Representations for LLM Vulnerability Reasoning
datasets: PrimeVul-derived corpus (107 Joern-based testcases, 30 projects, 5 CWE categories)

key_numbers.value: 69.4% at 12,938 avg tokens vs. 74.4% at 5,973 avg tokens

structure_gain: AST+PDG reaches 83.2% curated accuracy vs. 53.5% for raw source alone (+29.7pp), with model (qwen3.6-plus), temperature, prompting/checklist structure, and 50,000-character budget held fixed across all ten representation variants (§4.2, §5.2 Table 6)
confound_note: Model, temperature, prompting structure, and character budget are held constant across representation variants; program representation is the sole varied factor (§4.2) -- this is the study's central, deliberately isolated ablation
threats_to_datum: Modest corpus (107 testcases); CWE-190 dominates (56/107) while CWE-122 and CWE-191 have only 4 and 2 cases respectively (inadequate for category-level conclusions); single-model, single-run evaluation with acknowledged prompt-serialization and few-shot-selection bias (§7)

title: CLEAR: Causal Context-Based Agentic Reasoning for Vulnerability Detection
structure_gain: Full CLEAR (with Vulnerability Causal Knowledge Graph context) vs. No-VCKG ablation, same multi-agent LLM pipeline, on PrimeVul: Pairwise-Correct 19.17 vs. 8.08 (Table 3); removing only Fix-Intent nodes drops it to 14.32 vs. 19.17 full.
confound_note: Table 3's node-ablation removes individual VCKG node types (or the whole VCKG) while holding the multi-agent (Collector/Claim/Critic/Judge) architecture and base LLM fixed, isolating the causal-context representation's contribution; the headline 130.7%/71.56% figures instead compare CLEAR's full pipeline against a different prior system (VulTrial), which is not representation-isolated.
threats_to_datum: Authors note semantic similarity used to build VCKG edges does not guarantee causal consistency (nodes can be linked despite being causally unrelated, or left disconnected despite sharing a mechanism); human inter-rater agreement on Global Edge validity is only moderate (kappa=0.51); causal claims are LLM-derived, not symbolically verified.
